It’s perfectly all right if you don’t write often or at length; I just am glad to hear from you and know you and yours are okay. And I want to thank you for the pictures; we have the two of Willis up on the wall, where he can inspire us each morning to ferocity. 

I’m glad you’re more at home now, not down at the law office. Home is where I am all the time, even writing novels. So I can dig the trip; right on! Remember we once compared musical tastes and discovered we both were Linda Ronstadt freaks? I’m told now that the album, her first, that you and I both had, “Hand Sown ...” can’t be obtained by record stores. But listen: this area where I’m living is where Linda Ronstadt hangs out. A number of audio­ philes down here whom I’ve run into know her personally. She does a lot of small club and campus hall type singing ... they say now she’s changed a lot; once she sang wearing Levi’s and no shoes, but now it’s fancy gowns. I feel, from her two more recent records that she’s gone down hill, and I would recom­ mend to you Rita Coolidge. I think Rita Coolidge is filling in the vacuum that Linda Ronstadt left when she gave up the Levi’s. But you may know all this, so I will conclude. 

Cats are funny people. We have a big pink nothing of a tomcat, who has caught in his life one gopher and one mouse. When he caught the mouse he ran with it to his food dish and dropped it in, still live, because that is where he eats his food. The mouse ran off.
